I'm weighing whether an agent can be passed directly as a tool given the type mismatch between BidiAction and Action(I,O), and worrying that doing so would lose the sub-agent's session state. A cleaner approach seems to be building a dedicated delegating tool for each specialist instead.

For the refund case specifically, I'm stuck on how the approveRefund interrupt should propagate: if the refund tool calls into the sub-agent's chat and gets back interrupts, there's no obvious way to resume that sub-chat later for human approval without the delegating tool itself handling the interrupt somehow.

I shouldn't over-engineer this. Resuming a sub-agent's interrupt from within triage would require tracking sub-session state and re-invoking tools on resume, which is a lot of added complexity. Since there's no existing approval UI and refundAgent is already exported for callers to handle interrupts directly, I think the honest approach is to let callers who need refund approvals interact with refundAgent directly rather than trying to proxy interrupts through triage.

Instead, I'll have the delegating tool return text plus session info, so if a refund needs approval, triage can simply tell the customer it's pending and the approver can resume the refund session separately via refundAgent.loadChat. That keeps the approval gate intact without forcing triage to manage sub-agent interrupts itself, and I'll explain this as a deliberate design tradeoff to the user.

For persistence, I'm realizing triage needs access to the same session store so loadChat can later retrieve sessions by id — I should reuse the existing FileSessionStore instance already wired up for refundAgent rather than creating a separate one. Sub-agents without a store, like orderAgent, presumably rely on in-memory or client-managed chat state since we only use them for one-off delegated questions rather than resumable conversations.

I'm also thinking through how each delegation needs a self-contained question since sub-agents don't inherit history, so triage must embed the order id directly into whatever it asks downstream. For naming, I'll settle on handOffToOrderAgent and handOffToRefundAgent as clear tool names with descriptive handoff behavior in their descriptions.

I need to check how the library's response building handles interrupts from the refund approval flow — whether send() throws or just returns an interrupts field alongside finishReason — so I should peek at the agent implementation to confirm. I also want to verify AgentResponse exposes sessionId directly so triage's chat loop can read and persist it after each send, and that creating a chat with no sessionId simply establishes a new session on first call.

Finally, I'll add the triage export to index.ts and run a TypeScript typecheck to validate everything compiles, but since I don't have a model API key to actually exercise the full conversation flow, I'll note that I verified types and logic without a live end-to-end run.
